docRequirement: code-review.md:285 binds a user-invocable `/code-review` command that "reviews a diff in your terminal" and "reports correctness bugs and reuse, simplification, and efficiency cleanups". Its contract, one layer down the same page: default scope is "your branch's commits ahead of its upstream plus any uncommitted changes" (:295); a target may be "a file path, a PR number, a branch name, or a ref range such as `main...my-feature`" (:295); flags are `--fix` ("applies the findings to your working tree after the review") and `--comment` ("posts the findings as inline PR comments") (:299-:300); an effort level may precede them and absent it "the review uses the session's current effort" (:324); without `ultra` "everything left is the review target, even when it starts with another command name" (:328); the review "runs as a background subagent with its own context window" and falls back to the foreground when re-run while in progress, in `-p`/SDK mode, or when `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS` is `1` (:304, :333-:337); "When the host application requests it, Claude reports the review's findings through the `ReportFindings` tool" with a `category` tag such as `correctness` (:312); and the command "is marked `disable-model-invocation`" so a scheduled task reads it as plain text (:339). `/code-review ultra` escalates to cloud ultrareview and, when ultrareview is unavailable, "runs a local review in your session instead" (:343, :346). `/simplify` is the pre-v2.1.147 name and from v2.1.154 is a separate cleanup-only review (:353). :10 states the local command is available on every plan, so this is not a subscription-gated surface.

divergence: The review ENGINE exists and is wired; the documented ENTRY POINT and four contract details do not. (1) No user-invocable command: `review` is model-invocable only, the exact inverse of the doc's `disable-model-invocation` (:339). (2) Wrong default scope: ours is uncommitted-only (review-tool.ts:83) where the doc's is "branch's commits ahead of its upstream plus any uncommitted changes" (:295) — an upstream-relative diff we never compute. (3) Narrower target grammar: `base` (merge-base) and `commit` only; no file path, no PR number, no `main...my-feature` ref range, and no `ultra`. (4) No `--fix` and no `--comment`; `--comment` has no underlying GitHub mechanism anywhere in the repo. (5) Foreground-only: `background: false` is hard-coded (review-tool.ts:316), so the doc's background-subagent default and its three named foreground fallbacks are all collapsed into the fallback. (6) Findings ride a different shape: our P0-P3 `title/body/priority/confidence` object rendered as text, not `ReportFindings`' `file/summary/failureScenario/category` (:312) — same information, incompatible keys, and no `category` slug. (7) Cleanup findings absent: the rubric flags introduced defects only, where :285 also binds "reuse, simplification, and efficiency cleanups". (8) No per-invocation effort argument (:324). Also a fork-internal contradiction: our docs-site documents `/review` as a built-in slash command and no such command exists.

userImpact: Concrete and doubly bad, because our own docs advertise the missing command. A user reads docs-site/content/core-concepts/interactions.md:41 ("**`/review`** runs a dedicated, adversarial code review of a diff"), types `/review` in the composer, and nothing command-like happens: `/review` is not in the `/` menu (slash-command-menu.tsx:17), it is not a session command (session-command.ts:38-57), so the literal string is sent to the model as prose. `/code-review` behaves the same. Whether a review actually runs is then up to the model deciding to call the `review` tool on its own. When it does, the user gets a review that is narrower than the page they may have read: it covers only uncommitted changes — a user who has committed their branch work and typed `/code-review` expecting the documented "commits ahead of upstream" scope gets "No changes to review" — it blocks the turn instead of running in the background, it never applies its own fixes, it cannot take a PR number or a `main...my-feature` range, it reports no reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups, and its findings arrive as a P0-P3 text block rather than a rendered findings list.
